chunk_findings.detail: `_rounds` selects a single review gate as the gate “the rounds count over”, but the sample values count every RAN review verdict for the item across all gates in `review`. Given `PR.REVIEW_GATES` containing `rubber_duck` and `critic`, and a completed item with one passed `rubber_duck` verdict and two passed `critic` verdicts, `counts` makes `gate == "critic"`, while `values` for that item is `3`. The resulting `rounds` table therefore claims to count over `critic` but contains total review rounds over all review gates, overestimating the selected gate’s rounds whenever multiple review gates have verdicts.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/eta/data.py:_rounds

chunk_findings.detail: When there are no RAN review verdicts at all, `_rounds` still returns one zero sample per completed item instead of an empty sample list. Given one completed span and `facts.outcomes` empty, `counts` is empty, `gate` becomes `DEFAULT_REVIEW_GATE`, and `values` is `[0]`; `build` then creates `rounds.samples=[0.0]`, and with `min_samples=1` `apply_min_samples` reports `p50_s=0` and leaves `insufficient` empty. This contradicts the stated convention that “with no review verdicts at all ... the samples are empty” and turns “no review-round data” into a fabricated zero-round measurement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/eta/data.py:_rounds

chunk_findings.detail: The `lease.waiting` event is added with `log.add("lease.waiting", "W", "w1", T0, at=T0 - 600, ...)`, while every other event in this file passes the event timestamp as the fourth positional argument. Under the fixture’s `Log.add(event, item, actor, at, **data)` convention, this supplies `at` both positionally and as a keyword, so the test raises `TypeError: got multiple values for argument 'at'` before `ED.build` is reached. Even if the fixture accepts `at` as event data, the event’s own timestamp remains `T0`, so a wait-to-claim fold that uses the event timestamp would produce `0`, not the asserted `600`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_eta_data.py:test_lease_wait_is_first_wait_signal_to_first_claim

chunk_findings.detail: `_review_gate` chooses the review gate from every RAN review outcome in `facts.outcomes`, while `_rounds` then emits one sample for each completed span in the `spans`/rolling-window population passed to it. If a RAN review outcome exists only for an item outside that population (never completed, or outside the rolling window), the gate is still chosen and `_rounds` returns a zero for every in-window completed item that did not run that gate. For example, with `min_samples=1`, one completed span with no review verdicts plus one out-of-window/non-completed item with one `rubber_duck` RAN outcome makes `_review_gate` return `rubber_duck`, `_rounds` return `("rubber_duck", [0])`, and `build` produce `rounds.samples=[0.0]`; `apply_min_samples` then treats the table as having data and reports p50 `0` instead of marking it insufficient. The new test only covers the case where `facts.outcomes` has no review verdicts at all, so this fabricated-zero path remains.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/eta/data.py:_review_gate

chunk_findings.detail: The change moves `sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))` below the `from ddflow...` imports, so the repo root is inserted into `sys.path` only after those imports have already been resolved. In a source checkout where the repo root is not already first on `sys.path` (for example, running `python tests/test_eta_data.py`, where `sys.path[0]` is the `tests/` directory), this fails at `from ddflow.config import Config` with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ddflow'`. In an environment that has an older `ddflow` installed in site-packages, the test will instead import and exercise the installed package while `lanes_fixture` is loaded from the source tree, silently mixing versions; the previous placement before all local imports avoided both cases.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_eta_data.py:import block (`sys.path.insert` after `ddflow` imports)

chunk_findings.detail: In `gate_durations`, `key = (o.item, o.gate)` was removed from its original scope before the loop, but inside the loop `facts.starts.get(key, ())` was changed to `facts.starts.get((o.item, o.gate), ())`, leaving the name `key` unbound if any other code or subsequent refactoring references it. More critically, the loop over `outcomes` looks up `prev = max((x.at for x in outcomes if x.item == o.item and x.gate == o.gate and x.at < o.at), default=None)` for every outcome without regard to whether `o.item` belongs to `inside_items` (when `inside_items` is not None), yet `by_gate[o.gate].append(...)` only guards the item append at the top. This causes outcomes for items outside the rolling window to still be evaluated as potential `prev` verdicts for items inside the window, distorting the calculation of `began` and gate durations when an item outside the window shared a gate name and had a verdict just before an item inside the window.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/eta/data.py:99

chunk_findings.detail: `build` computes `inside` and uses it to window cycles, lease waits, and rounds, but it passes the full `facts` to `gate_durations(facts)`. Given `eta.window_days=1` and a synthetic log containing 100 `gate.started`/`gate.passed` pairs for gate `critic` from 100 days ago and no gate verdicts in the last day, `gate_durations(facts)` still returns 100 samples, so `Tables.gate_durations[0].samples_summary["p50_s"]` is a stale number and `insufficient` does not name `critic`. Thus the rolling-window knob does not limit gate-duration statistics, contradicting the intent that the ETA read model is windowed and that “insufficient data” is reported when there are no in-window samples.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/eta/data.py:build

chunk_findings.detail: The review gate is chosen with `max(review, key=lambda g: per_gate[g])`, where `review` can be a set (the fallback `{"rubber_duck", "critic"}` or a set-valued `PR.REVIEW_GATES`). If two review gates tie for most RAN verdicts, `max` returns an arbitrary element of the set iteration order, which is not stable across processes for string sets. For example, with `PR.REVIEW_GATES` empty/None and two completed items, one having one `rubber_duck` verdict and the other one `critic` verdict, `Tables.rounds.gate` and `Tables.rounds.samples` can differ between runs (e.g. `[1, 0]` vs `[0, 1]`), making the derived read model nondeterministic.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/eta/data.py:_review_gate

chunk_findings.detail: The test logs the wait signal with `log.add("lease.waiting", "W", "w1", T0, at=T0 - 600, ...)`, while the claim is at `T0`. In the other `log.add` calls in this file, the fourth positional argument is the event timestamp, so the `lease.waiting` event is recorded at `T0`, not `T0 - 600`; the assertion expects a 600-second wait. If `lanes_fixture.Log.add` uses the common signature `add(event, task, lease, at, **fields)`, this call is also invalid because `at` is supplied both positionally and as a keyword (`TypeError: got multiple values for argument 'at'`). Either way, this test cannot reliably demonstrate a 600-second lease wait; the event should be logged at `T0 - 600` as the event timestamp.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_eta_data.py:test_lease_wait_is_first_wait_signal_to_first_claim
